name: Scleral Photooxidative Ablation Pistol
description:
The Scleral Photooxidative Ablation Pistol fires a precisely collimated burst of high-intensity ultraviolet-A and visible violet light specifically tuned to the absorption spectrum of melanin in the retinal pigment epithelium. The burst triggers a cascade of reactive oxygen species generation within the photoreceptor layer, causing immediate and irreversible photooxidative destruction of the macular region. The target experiences a silent, painless flash followed by a central scotoma — a permanent blind spot that expands over the following six hours as the oxidative cascade propagates through adjacent tissue.

The SPAP-4's distinctive design feature is its pre-flash pupil dilation module: a brief sub-threshold pulse of specific wavelengths causes involuntary pupillary dilation in the target half a second before the ablative burst fires, maximizing the amount of destructive light energy that penetrates to the retina. This dilation response is hardwired into the autonomic nervous system and cannot be consciously suppressed. Standard anti-laser eyewear with fixed tint provides reduced but not full protection; only active photochromic lenses with response times under 0.3 milliseconds offer meaningful defense, and few civilians own them.

The weapon was developed by Helix Biosystems under contract for use in riot suppression as a 'non-lethal incapacitant,' a classification that has been widely and bitterly contested. Critics note that permanent bilateral blindness is not meaningfully non-lethal in the context of GLMZ's streets. The pistol form factor makes it easily concealable, and the silent operation — just a faint violet flash — has made it a weapon of choice for quiet crowd control and targeted political intimidation.
specifications:
effective range: 2–25 meters
pre flash dilation pulse: 0.5 seconds prior to ablative burst
ablative burst duration: 8 milliseconds
wavelength bands: 365nm UVA primary, 415nm violet secondary
power source: Compact photonic cell, 22 shots per charge
weight: 0.9 kg
form factor: Pistol, 19cm overall length
countermeasure: Active photochromic lenses <0.3ms response time
tactical_use: Deployed in crowd dispersal to permanently blind designated agitators or leadership figures as a deterrent measure. In covert operations, used to silently incapacitate targets in a way that appears accidental or is attributed to industrial UV exposure. Operators in close-quarters situations appreciate the pistol's compactness and the fact that the flash is easily mistaken for camera equipment or a phone screen in a crowd. Some enforcement units carry the SPAP-4 as a secondary weapon specifically for taking out targets who are augmented against conventional firearms.
cultural_context: The SPAP-4 has become a symbol of state violence in GLMZ's civil rights discourse. After several documented uses against protesters in the Outer Ring districts, the weapon's violet flash became an iconographic image in anti-corporate art — reproduced on murals, tattoos, and protest flags as a symbol of state-inflicted permanent harm. Survivors who were blinded by the weapon and received no compensation are called 'Whiteouts' in activist circles, and their community is one of the city's most organized political forces. Law enforcement officers who carry the SPAP-4 are sometimes identified and publicly named by underground data brokers.
known_users: Underground fixers with law enforcement connections
story_hooks: A data broker offers a fixer the identity list of every officer issued a SPAP-4 in the last two years — someone is planning something with that list, and the fixer has to decide whether to sell it, suppress it, or warn the officers.

A Helix Biosystems whistleblower claims the SPAP-4 was deliberately mislabeled as non-lethal despite internal studies showing high mortality rates among blinded subjects in GLMZ's streets — the evidence is encoded in a product lot number.
A Whiteout activist who was blinded by a SPAP-4 has somehow acquired several units and is threatening to use them on the corporate board members of Helix — but the players are hired by both sides.
A black market SPAP-4 modified for full bilateral blindness at 40 meters is found at the scene of a judicial assassination — someone is escalating.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist pistol with an unusually large, translucent barrel assembly housing optical components. The design is angular and clinical, resembling medical instrumentation more than traditional weaponry. The barrel dominates the profile—a prismatic crystalline tube mounted above the grip, giving it an top-heavy but deliberately balanced appearance.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 19cm. Barrel assembly: 8cm long, 2.5cm diameter. Grip: 8cm length. Width at widest point: 4.5cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light at 0.9kg—the photonic cell and optical components keep it from feeling substantial, almost insubstantial in hand despite its clinical presence. Balanced slightly forward due to the barrel's optical mass.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite with embedded carbon lattice for structural integrity. Barrel assembly is precision-ground fused silica with internal dichroic coatings. Grip and trigger guard are brushed anodized aluminum.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer body with a faint iridescent sheen suggesting internal optical complexity. Barrel has a subtle purple-tinted translucency revealing geometric optical elements within. Aluminum components are satin-finished with micro-abrasion marks from field handling.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal black primary body with deep violet accents around the barrel collar. Internal components visible as faint geometric purple light paths within the transparent barrel housing. Orange-tinted photonic cell indicator strip along the right grip.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with subtle grip fins, slightly tacky composite finish designed to prevent perspiration slipping. Trigger guard is knurled bare aluminum, cold to the touch.
distinctive_features: Translucent barrel assembly revealing internal dichroic optical stack
Integrated violet-tinted photonic cell window on the right grip
Subtle LED status indicators (cyan for ready, amber for low charge) near the rear sight
Pre-flash calibration lens—a faint iris-like aperture visible at barrel crown
Minimal mechanical trigger—nearly silent actuation mechanism
Geometric alignment guides etched into the barrel housing in clinical white
No visible muzzle flash signature—designed for invisibility
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS logo in white block lettering on the left grip panel. Regulatory serial number etched beneath: SPAP-4 / UV-CERT-CLASS-3. Small biohazard symbol next to manufacturer ID. Clinical product code stamped on barrel collar in serif font.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show minimal wear despite frequent deployment—polymer resists scratching, and operators maintain optics obsessively. Some units show faint purple residue on the barrel from improper cleaning solvents. Trigger mechanisms remain pristine, as there is minimal mechanical friction. Law enforcement examples often have department markings or unit tape; black market variants are usually unmarked with tampered serial numbers.
